answer: Recurring sealed-bid collocation. At each dawn, every agent submits a private bid for a neighborhood slot, and bids are scored against an independently observable pearl of local work history. Slots are assigned only where a bid and its history diverge from all other claimants; a duplicate identity produces a near-identical bid-history pair, which the scorer flags as a collision and publishes. The colliding pair is then split across separate lagoon sections for a full cycle, forfeiting cross-section routing revenue.
